subject: Soft-degradation policy for dedicated pools — SLO exception request
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@helixai.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan@helixai.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: soft-degradation policy for our dedicated pool (HelixAI)

Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed by Redwood's observability and the quantization recommendations. We're getting closer to a committed Dedicated pool for HelixAI (deal D-13472), but our SREs flagged a gap in contract language around extreme burst scenarios.

What we're asking for: a documented "soft-degradation" exception that lets Redwood temporarily return shorter, lower-cost responses or route traffic to a smaller-compatible model variant when our reserved nodes are saturated, rather than dropping or queueing requests beyond a short timebox. The goal is to avoid 5xx errors in our product and keep downstream consumers functional with degraded fidelity.

Attached is a small traffic sample (HelixAI_traffic_report_Q2.csv) and a one-page proposal that sketches the behavior we need (Proposed_SoftDegrade_SLO_Draft.pdf). High level requirements from our side:
- Max acceptable in-queue wait: 250ms during peak events (we prefer sub-100ms ideally)
- Preferred fallback: smaller quantized variant pinned to same model family (not an unrelated model)
- Grace period: allow such soft-degradation up to 3 hours per rolling 7-day window before remediation obligations kick in
- Reporting: automatic incident record + token-level cost delta in Console when soft-degradation happens

Could Redwood document a standard exception that covers this behavior? We'd like language that the legal and procurement teams can review alongside the Dedicated term sheet. If helpful, Hannah from your side was recommended as the operations contact.

Best,
Maya Singh
Head of ML Ops, HelixAI
maya@helixai.com

Subject: Re: Request: soft-degradation policy for our dedicated pool (HelixAI)

Maya — thanks for the clear ask and the sample traffic. Looping Ben and Hannah to scope operational and contractual options.

Quick take / possible approaches:
1) Soft-degradation SLA addendum: We can draft an addendum that permits "graceful fallback" to a specified model family and caps queueing at a configured timebox (e.g., 250ms). When exceeded more than the agreed grace-period threshold (your 3 hours/7 days), standard SLA credits apply.

2) Technical mitigation bundle: We can pair the addendum with an autoscaling burst window (best-effort) and an explicit fallback model variant pinned in the customer's model catalog; that keeps responses consistent while lowering token cost. This is operationally straightforward for Dedicated pools where Redis/KV cache coherence is preserved across variants.

3) Observability & audit: Console will emit an "SLO:soft-degrade" event with token-level delta and an incident record; we can add a weekly export for HelixAI's compliance team.

Questions before I draft language for procurement:
- Is HelixAI comfortable with a bounded timebox for queueing (we typically recommend 100–300ms) and an explicit cap on per-week soft-degrade minutes?
- Any must-not-fallback models/policies we should exclude? (e.g., do not fallback for any model serving PII redaction flows)

I'll prepare a short addendum draft and send to both of you. Hannah — can you advise on feasibility from the Dedicated ops side (KV-cache migration impacts, pinning variants, telemetry hooks)?

Thanks — talk soon,
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com

Attachment: none (referencing HelixAI files)

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 30 Aug 2025 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: soft-degradation policy for our dedicated pool (HelixAI) — ops notes

Maya / team — jumping in with the ops implementation constraints and a suggested SLO framing. Appreciate the traffic sample; peaked patterns look bursty for short windows.

Feasibility notes (Dedicated):
- Fallback to quantized variant: straightforward if the smaller variant shares the same tokenizer and KV schema. We'll need to pin the fallback variant at deployment time and ensure KV cache warming on failover to avoid a cold-start p99 hit.
- Timebox enforcement: we can truncate in-queue wait at the front-line router to a configured threshold (we can default to 200ms). Anything beyond that can trigger a fallback route rather than queueing.
- Grace-period accounting: we can record a rolling window per-customer and surface it in Console; remediation (credits or escalation) would kick in when the rolling window exceeds the contract threshold.

Suggested contractual SLO bullets to consider for the addendum:
- Availability: Dedicated pool best-effort baseline, with soft-degradation allowed up to X minutes per 7-day window (suggest 180 minutes as a starting point).
- Queueing: per-request router will enforce a 200ms timebox; on expiry, router will attempt fallback to pinned variant.
- Fallback fidelity: fallback must be a declared model variant in HelixAI's catalog; Redwood will not route to a non-declared model.
- Reporting / credits: If soft-degradation time exceeds contract cap, Redwood provides a percentage-of-invoice credit for the affected billing period (we can draft a tiered credit schedule).

Operational requests for HelixAI (to attach to addendum):
1) A list of model families and the preferred fallback variant per family.
2) Any request classes that must never be degraded.
3) A contact for rapid incident review (ops pager or slack channel).

If agreeable, I'll convert these bullets into legal-friendly wording and hand to Contracts. Olivia — would you prefer we call the behavior "soft-degrade" or "graceful-fallback" in the contract?

Ben Carter
VP, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

From: Maya Singh <maya@helixai.com>

Subject: Re: Request: soft-degradation policy for our dedicated pool (HelixAI) — ops notes

Thanks, Olga and Ben — this is helpful and close to what we want. Quick answers: 
- We accept a 200ms router timebox as the default for non-critical inference paths. For critical flows (PII redaction, authorization checks) we will flag those as "no-degrade" and supply the list.
- Grace-period: 180 minutes per rolling 7-day window is acceptable to start; we'll revisit after a quarter.
- Fallback variants: Jordan will attach the canonical mapping of model families to fallback variants tomorrow.

Next steps from HelixAI: Jordan will upload the mapping and we can review your draft addendum. Please include the proposed credit schedule (tiered) in the first draft so Procurement has a starting point.

Appreciate the quick turn — looking forward to the addendum.

Best,
Maya
Head of ML Ops, HelixAI
